title: Live demand map for a ride service

hook.shape: Demand spikes in one small spot while supply sits scattered far away, so showing the live picture becomes the problem.

arc: hook → numbered steps that build a live map → named traps inside a step → scaling comparison → callback ending

beats.summary: A crowd suddenly wants rides in one spot while the cars are spread far away, shown as a rising count over a map.
A moving vehicle's phone emits position records; they pile onto one server until it strains, then wait on a belt.
A grid is dropped over the map and one vehicle's coordinates turn into the single cell that holds it.
The map becomes a grid of numbers; a vehicle crossing a boundary lowers the old cell and raises the new one.
A parked vehicle keeps sending pings so its cell count inflates; the fix stores each driver's last cell and updates only on change.
A vehicle loses signal, a countdown ring runs out and its contribution is removed from the cell.
The same number grid is redrawn as a density view so crowding reads at a glance.
The single map splits into several regional maps, each wired to its own server.
Two cell shapes are compared on the same map for what neighbouring distance looks like in each.
One overloaded cell raises the price on a generic app screen, then a failed search state lands as the closing joke.

pacing: Hook lands fast: demand spike and distant cars in the opening seconds.
Each step stays short and ends on one visible change to the same map board.
The two traps slow the rhythm, then the comparison and the closing joke rush out.
